steps.b:
Chemistry studies matter (materija) — anything that has mass and takes up space — and how it changes.

A pure substance (čista supstanca) has a fixed composition and fixed properties, like a melting point. There are two kinds:

  • Elements (elementi) are made of one kind of atom: O₂, Fe, Cu.
  • Compounds (jedinjenja) are two or more elements chemically bonded in a fixed ratio: H₂O, NaCl, CaCO₃.
A fruit salad is a mixture — you can pick the pieces apart. A cake is like a compound — you can’t get the eggs back.

A mixture (smeša) contains two or more substances that keep their own properties and can be present in any ratio.

  • Homogeneous (homogena) mixtures look the same everywhere: salt water, air, brass. Solutions are homogeneous mixtures.
  • Heterogeneous (heterogena) mixtures have visible parts: sand in water, muddy water, granite.
Geology link: granite is a heterogeneous mixture of minerals — quartz, feldspar and mica. Each mineral on its own is a compound with a fixed formula, like quartz, SiO₂.

Mixtures are separated by physical methods, using differences in properties:

  • Filtration (ceđenje): an insoluble solid from a liquid — sand from water.
  • Evaporation (uparavanje): a dissolved solid from its solution — salt from sea water.
  • Distillation (destilacija): liquids with different boiling points, or pure water from salt water.
  • Decanting (dekantovanje): pouring the liquid off a settled solid.
  • Magnet: iron from a mixture.

A physical change doesn’t make new substances (melting ice, dissolving sugar). A chemical change does (burning, rusting).

steps.q: How would you separate a mixture of sand, salt and iron filings?
s: Pull out the iron filings with a magnet.
Add water: the salt dissolves, the sand doesn’t.
Filter: the sand stays on the filter paper.
Evaporate the water from the filtrate: salt remains.

steps.q: Which of these is a compound?
steps.e: Water is two elements (H and O) bonded in a fixed 2:1 ratio. O₂ and Fe are elements, air is a mixture.
Air is a homogeneous mixture of N₂, O₂, Ar, CO₂ and other gases.
You can see separate grains of quartz, feldspar and mica.

steps.q: Which method gives pure water from sea water?
steps.e: Water boils off and condenses; the salt stays behind. Filtration can’t remove dissolved salt.
Burning makes new substances (CO₂, H₂O, ash).
